title: Chinamaxxing: Drinking Hot Water Isn't a Hack in China — It's the Tap | China Travel Expert
description:
On TikTok, the 'Chinamaxxing' or 'becoming Chinese' trend has people copying Chinese habits — including sipping plain hot or warm water as if it were a wellness secret. In China it isn't a hack at all. Boiled water, kaishui (kāi shuǐ), is simply what people drink, and the habit goes back to public-health campaigns about a century ago: boil your water and you are far less likely to get sick. It's also free almost everywhere — train stations, airports, offices and schools have hot-water dispensers, and every long-distance train car has its own hot-water tap. So: ancient wellness secret, or just free hot water?

★ Expert Tip: Travelling in China, carry an empty insulated bottle. You'll find free boiling-water dispensers in every train station and on every train — handy for tea, instant noodles, or just a warm drink on a cold platform.

在 TikTok 上，「Chinamaxxing（变得更中国）」潮流让很多人模仿中国人的习惯，其中之一就是把喝热水、温水当成养生秘诀。在中国这根本不是什么妙招。喝开水（kāi shuǐ，烧开过的水）就是日常，这个习惯大约一个世纪前就随公共卫生运动流行起来：水烧开了，就不容易生病。而且几乎到处都免费——火车站、机场、办公室、学校都有饮水机，每节长途列车车厢都有自己的热水口。那么：这是古老的养生秘诀，还是单纯的免费热水？

—
I'm mapping ALL of China — real streets, real history, zero tourist traps.

Facts verified 2026-11-25:
• Drinking boiled, hot or warm water is a long-standing Chinese custom tied to 20th-century public-health campaigns (the Republic-era New Life Movement and the 1952 Patriotic Health Campaign promoted boiling water to prevent waterborne disease) — Atlas Obscura, 'Are China's Days of Hot Drinking Water Over?' https://www.atlasobscura.com/articles/china-hot-drinking-water-traditional-medicine + Goldthread / SCMP, 'Why do Chinese people love drinking hot water?' https://www.goldthread2.com/culture/why-chinese-people-drink-hot-water/article/3084579
• Free boiled/hot water is widely available in public places in China — train stations, airports, offices and schools have dispensers, and each long-distance train carriage has a hot-water tap — TravelChinaGuide, 'China Train Facilities' https://www.travelchinaguide.com/china-trains/facilities.htm + Atlas Obscura (above)
• The 'Chinamaxxing' / 'turning Chinese' trend (copying Chinese habits such as drinking hot water) spread on TikTok in 2026 — Fortune, 'What is becoming Chinese / Chinamaxxing' https://fortune.com/2026/04/19/what-is-becoming-chinese-chinamaxxing-tiktok-trend-american-critique/ + NBC News, 'turning Chinese trend' https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/viral/turning-chinese-trend-tiktok-social-media-rcna255478

es.title: Chinamaxxing: beber agua caliente no es un truco en China, es el grifo
es.description: En TikTok, la moda 'Chinamaxxing' hace que la gente copie hábitos chinos, como beber agua caliente cual secreto de bienestar. En China no es ningún truco: el agua hervida (kaishui) es lo que se bebe, y viene de campañas de salud pública de hace un siglo. Además es gratis casi en todas partes: estaciones, oficinas, escuelas y cada vagón de tren tienen agua caliente. ¿Secreto milenario, o simplemente agua caliente gratis?

pt.title: Chinamaxxing: beber água quente não é truque na China, é a torneira
pt.description: No TikTok, a moda 'Chinamaxxing' faz as pessoas copiarem hábitos chineses, como beber água quente como se fosse um segredo de bem-estar. Na China não é truque nenhum: água fervida (kaishui) é o que se bebe, e vem de campanhas de saúde pública de um século atrás. E é grátis em quase todo lugar: estações, escritórios, escolas e cada vagão de trem têm água quente. Segredo milenar, ou só água quente de graça?

id.title: Chinamaxxing: minum air panas bukan trik di China — itu air keran
id.description: Di TikTok, tren 'Chinamaxxing' membuat orang meniru kebiasaan China, termasuk menyeruput air panas seolah rahasia kesehatan. Di China itu bukan trik: air matang (kaishui) memang minuman sehari-hari, warisan kampanye kesehatan seabad lalu. Dan gratis hampir di mana saja: stasiun, kantor, sekolah, dan tiap gerbong kereta punya keran air panas. Rahasia kuno, atau sekadar air panas gratis?

hi.title: Chinamaxxing: चीन में गरम पानी पीना कोई हैक नहीं — वह तो नल है
hi.description: टिकटॉक पर 'Chinamaxxing' ट्रेंड में लोग चीनी आदतें अपना रहे हैं, जैसे गरम पानी पीना मानो कोई सेहत का राज़ हो। चीन में यह हैक नहीं है: उबला पानी (kaishui) यहाँ रोज़ का पेय है, और यह आदत करीब सौ साल पुराने जन-स्वास्थ्य अभियानों से आई। और यह लगभग हर जगह मुफ़्त है — स्टेशन, दफ़्तर, स्कूल और हर ट्रेन डिब्बे में गरम पानी का नल। पुराना राज़, या बस मुफ़्त गरम पानी?

ar.title: تشايناماكسينغ: شرب الماء الساخن ليس حيلة في الصين — إنه الصنبور
ar.description: على تيك توك تدفع موضة 'تشايناماكسينغ' الناس لتقليد العادات الصينية، ومنها احتساء الماء الساخن وكأنه سرّ صحي. في الصين ليس حيلة: الماء المغلي (كايشوي) هو ما يُشرب أصلاً، وهذه عادة تعود لحملات صحية عامة قبل نحو قرن. وهو مجاني في كل مكان تقريباً — المحطات والمكاتب والمدارس، ولكل عربة قطار صنبور ماء ساخن. سرّ قديم، أم مجرد ماء ساخن مجاني؟

fr.title: Chinamaxxing : boire de l'eau chaude n'est pas une astuce en Chine, c'est le robinet
fr.description: Sur TikTok, la mode 'Chinamaxxing' pousse à copier les habitudes chinoises, dont boire de l'eau chaude comme un secret bien-être. En Chine, ce n'est pas une astuce : l'eau bouillie (kaishui) est ce qu'on boit, héritage de campagnes de santé publique d'il y a un siècle. Et c'est gratuit presque partout : gares, bureaux, écoles, et chaque voiture de train a son robinet d'eau chaude. Secret ancestral, ou simplement de l'eau chaude gratuite ?
